flashcard_questions.q: What does Tawhid mean in Muslim belief?
flashcard_questions.a: The oneness of Allah — one God, eternal, with no partners or children.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Malaikah in the Six Articles of Faith?
flashcard_questions.a: Belief in angels, created from light, who carry out Allah’s commands perfectly.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Kutub in the Six Articles of Faith?
flashcard_questions.a: Belief in the holy books that Allah revealed to his prophets.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Al-Qadr in the Six Articles?
flashcard_questions.a: Predestination — Allah knows everything that has happened and will happen.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Adalat in Shi’a belief?
flashcard_questions.a: Divine justice — Allah is perfectly just and never acts unfairly.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Al-Ma’ad in Shi’a belief?
flashcard_questions.a: Resurrection — every person will be physically raised and judged by Allah.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Iman in Sunni Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: The Arabic term for faith, covering the six core beliefs.

flashcard_questions.q: What is shirk in Islamic teaching?
flashcard_questions.a: Associating partners with Allah — the worst sin in Islam.

flashcard_questions.q: Who did most Muslims choose as Caliph after Muhammad’s death?
Who did the Shi’a believe should have led the community after Muhammad?
flashcard_questions.a: Ali, the Prophet’s cousin and son-in-law.

flashcard_questions.q: When did the Prophet Muhammad die?
Which Shi’a root of faith has no equivalent in Sunni Islam?
What proportion of Muslims worldwide are Sunni?
Which surah declares “He is Allah, the One”?

notes: 15 cards: 8 article/root→definition (Tawhid, Malaikah, Kutub, Al-Qadr, Adalat, Al-Ma’ad, Iman, Usul ad-Din), 1 term→definition (shirk), 3 person/leadership cards (Abu Bakr, Ali, the Imamate), 1 date card (632 CE), 1 statistic (80–90% Sunni), 1 belief→source (Surah 112). Risalah and Nubuwwah dropped to avoid interference with each other in the same deck.
